clue.text: Ely pubs set out to entertain royal very well indeed

indicators.note: a host who entertains a guest holds them inside, so one piece goes within the other
things set out are laid out afresh, so the letters of the town and the bars are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the cathedral city and the bars, taken as written
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN or RA

explanation.surface: The pubs of Ely make a fine show when hosting a royal visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Superbly is an adverb meaning excellently, so it matches the intensified phrase for doing something well.

clue.text: Promotion for special drinks on sports field

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
ales are beers, drinks
a pitch is a playing field for football or cricket

explanation.surface: An advertisement for specially priced drinks at the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales pitch is the persuasive talk used to promote and sell a product.

clue.text: Socket for a presentation system?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wall outlet supplying electricity

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks what you plug a projector into; the answer is both the outlet and the software.
explanation.definitionFit: A power point is a British term for an electrical outlet, and PowerPoint is a widely used slideshow program.

clue.text: Limerick, say, by Frost, say

indicators.note: say asks us to hear the word spoken rather than read its spelling

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, an icy coating on plants

explanation.surface: A limerick written by the poet Robert Frost, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the American poet; it is ice. The first 'say' marks an example, the second a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A limerick is one kind of rhyme, a short comic verse, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: All's done in preparation for punch that wins boxing trophy

indicators.note: things in preparation are being made ready and reorganised, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written
a belt is a hard blow

explanation.surface: Everything is set for the knockout blow that takes the title.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lonsdale Belt is the championship belt of British professional boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lonsdale Belt is awarded to British boxing champions, a prize trophy in that sport.

clue.text: Tipsy chemist imbibing spirit

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so the two words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A drunken pharmacist is helping himself to the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like the drink being imbibed, but it is the soul or mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, which is one sense of spirit.

clue.text: Flags put up next to A roads

parts.note: to stand something is to put it up
taken as written
RDS is the abbreviation for roads

explanation.surface: Banners are hoisted beside the main roads.
explanation.walkthrough: A roads are Britain's main roads, below motorways; here the A is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, especially one carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Setter in jail with 23's killer

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler is locked up alongside a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the Old Testament character in 23 down; in Genesis he was killed by his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain murdered his brother Abel, according to the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Life peer's sword?

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.walkthrough: There is no indicator word; the question mark hints the answer lurks within. A life peer is a member of the House of Lords whose title is not inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a sword used in fencing, with a stiff blade.

clue.text: Dishonesty found at base just above sea level

parts.note: base and low both mean mean or contemptible
telling untruths is dishonesty

explanation.surface: Deceit is discovered at the root of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The dishonesty sits at the end, after the base, giving LOW-LYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-lying land is close to sea level, barely raised above the tides.

clue.text: Father's written about a primarily Trollopian literary genre

indicators.note: something written about another is written around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily points to the first, so only the opening letter of the novelist's name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Dad has written about a Trollope-style genre of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Trollope was a Victorian novelist; Father's here means father is.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is a genre of writing that uses ridicule and irony to mock vice or folly.

clue.text: Angry former partner has a fund to question a witness for the other side

definitions.text: question a witness for the other side

parts.note: cross means annoyed
an ex is a former partner
taken as written
a mine is a rich source or fund, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: A furious ex has money to grill a hostile witness.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross-examine is to interrogate a witness called by the opposing side in a trial.

clue.text: Gave in to Russia, backing split with alliance's last communist

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is read from its end

parts.note: RUS is a standard abbreviation for Russia
to rend is to tear or split

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word
red is a common label for a communist

explanation.surface: Someone yielded to Russia, supporting a split alongside the alliance's final communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give in, so the past tense matches 'gave in'.

clue.text: I get meal reinstated, maintaining it's kosher

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the rearranged letters hold the other word
reinstated suggests things restated or put back differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner insists the dish restored to them is fit to eat under Jewish law.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosher is informally used to mean genuine or above board, which is what legitimate means.

clue.text: Work memo with plenty changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office note has been heavily revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment is paid work, a job or occupation.

clue.text: Prepares clothes for use on the golf course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: presses garments smooth with a hot appliance

definitions.text: for use on the golf course
definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: metal-headed clubs carried by a golfer

explanation.surface: Someone gets their outfit ready for a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them smooth, and irons are also a family of golf clubs.

clue.text: Flooded planet almost reaching unfortunate date

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deluged world is nearing a doomed day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saturated is soaked through, holding as much water as it can, as flooded ground does.

clue.text: Amber ales brewed to exhibit a high-intensity ray

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A brewery makes golden beers that shine brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a narrow, concentrated ray of coherent light of great intensity.

clue.text: Artist in copper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., the English landscape painter
second meaning: a police officer, copper being slang for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' tempts toward an artist working in metal; it is British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable painted The Hay Wain, and a constable is the lowest police rank in Britain.

clue.text: Quiet place to make drink

definitions.meaning: second meaning: apparatus for distilling spirits

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot where one brews alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means calm or silent, and a still is the apparatus in which whisky and other spirits are distilled.

clue.text: Lie and try alibi about trustworthiness

indicators.note: about suggests turning things round and moving them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspect fibs and attempts an alibi concerning their honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that lying and alibis are the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliability is the quality of being dependable, which is what trustworthiness means.

clue.text: Mad old tax collector put away

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, replaced by HMRC in 2005
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: An angry former taxman has been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests imprisonment; it means eaten. The Inland Revenue was the British tax authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in its informal sense of angry is a synonym for irate.

clue.text: Make something to sit on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to create or shape
second meaning: a long backless bench

explanation.walkthrough: A form is a long wooden bench, as in an old school classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To form something is to make it, and a form is also a backless bench seat.

clue.text: Old Testament character without Latin name

parts.note: Abe is a man's name, short for Abraham
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A biblical figure lacks a Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense of 'outside' it puts Latin outside the name, at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel is the second son of Adam and Eve in Genesis, part of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Circulates gold coins

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
bits are small coins, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Gold coins are passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel round and round something, which is what circulating means.

clue.text: Verger initially in charge, with a passion for the boss's house?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the church officer is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
taken as written
a rage is a violent passion

explanation.surface: A church verger takes charge with zeal for his superior's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: A verger is a church caretaker, and the vicar is his boss; the question mark admits the definition is oblique.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a parish vicar, the person a verger works under.

clue.text: Month in which boy gets sickness

indicators.note: in which says the following word goes inside the one before it

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: There is a month in which a young lad falls ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or disease, a formal word for sickness.

clue.text: Principle restricting males to very basic accommodation

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one word closes around the other

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men are males

explanation.surface: A rule confines men to the most spartan lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a run-down building divided into cheap flats, typically poor, crowded housing.
